claims.quote: It is currently considered a monogenic X-linked dominant disorder due to mutations in MECP2 gene
A few RTT male cases, resulting from mosaicism for MECP2 mutations, have been reported.

claims.object_text: severe encephalopathy with death at birth; X-linked recessive mental retardation (XLMR)
claims.quote: Male germline MECP2 mutations cause either severe encephalopathy with death at birth (usually in brothers of classical RTT females) or X-linked recessive mental retardation (XLMR).
MECP2 mutations account for approximately 70-80% of classic RTT cases.
MeCP2 is considered a general transcriptional repressor.
The involvement of MeCP2 in methylation-specific transcriptional repression suggests that MECP2 related disorders result from dysregulated gene expression.

claims.object_text: conditional mouse mutants with selective loss of Mecp2 in the brain
claims.quote: conditional mouse mutants with selective loss of Mecp2 in the brain develop clinical manifestations similar to RTT

claims.object_text: required for central nervous system function
claims.quote: MECP2 is exclusively required for central nervous system function.

claims.object_text: a relatively small number of gene expression changes
claims.quote: A relatively small number of gene expression changes were identified.

claims.object_text: digenic model in which a mutated allele in a second gene determines clinical severity
claims.quote: we propose a digenic model in which the presence of a "mutated" allele in a second gene, leading to a less functional protein, determines the clinical severity of the MECP2 mutation.
